---
title: "Example SIRDS model"
---

We use a stochastic SIRDS (Susceptible–Infected–Recovered–Dead–Susceptible)
compartmental model as a running example throughout the docs. The particulars of how this model work aren't too important, but the basic idea is that our simulator depends on some static input parameters (I0, beta, etc...) and produces stochastic timeseries of compartment counts over time.

## Code definition

The canonical implementation is imported from the installed package. It advances
counts in discrete steps (default one day), using binomial infection/waning draws
and a multinomial recovery/death/stay draw. Population size defaults to 1000;
`I0` fixes the initial infected fraction and the four rates are supplied inputs,
not parameters inferred in this example. Recovery and death probabilities are
`1-exp(-rate*dt)` and must sum to at most one. This preserves the original tutorial's
discrete competing-risk approximation; it is not an exact continuous-time process.
All displayed variation comes from process draws at fixed inputs.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


from metis.datasets.sirds import simulate_sirds
```


## Example realisations

Here we again emphasise that even with fixed input parameters, varying the random seed produces different realisations.
```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(10, 4.5))
for s in range(20):
    S, I, R, D = simulate_sirds(seed=s)
    t = np.arange(len(S))
    ax.plot(t, S, color="#2E86AB", label="S" if s == 0 else None, alpha=0.35, lw=1)
    ax.plot(t, I, color="#C73E1D", label="I" if s == 0 else None, alpha=0.35, lw=1)
    ax.plot(t, R, color="#6A994E", label="R" if s == 0 else None, alpha=0.35, lw=1)
    ax.plot(t, D, color="#C21B8A", label="D" if s == 0 else None, alpha=0.35, lw=1)
ax.set(
    xlabel="time (days)",
    ylabel="count",
    title="",
)
ax.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
